title: A Message Cannot Arrive Before It Is Sent: physical-consistency auditing for streaming latency benchmarks

creators.name: Ricou, Gustavo Pedro
creators.affiliation: School of Computer Science and Statistics, Trinity College Dublin, Dublin, Ireland

description:
Code, measurements, analysis and paper for a study of measurement validity in streaming latency benchmarks.

We set out to compare Apache Kafka and Redis Streams for a real-time sports data feed and obtained a clean, statistically strong, theory-confirming answer. It was physically impossible: broker transport subtracts a timestamp taken in the producer process from one taken in the consumer process, and a check against that causal constraint rejected 1,321 of 2,266 runs, including every run behind the headline result.

The archive contains the consistency check itself, the full audit including the rejected corpus, the surviving comparison, and a regression suite that recomputes every figure in the paper from committed data and fails if paper and data disagree.

Data note. No StatsBomb event data is redistributed here. Replay plans derived from it are excluded from this record and are regenerable byte-for-byte from a pinned upstream commit using the included scripts. Aggregate workload statistics computed from that dataset are included and remain subject to StatsBomb's CC BY-NC 4.0 terms with attribution; all code and all latency measurements are MIT.
